gates.claim: NON-VACUITY, the gate class that caught correction 6: all SIX VSide conditions hold SIMULTANEOUSLY at every root at every arc point. The earlier version of this hypothesis carried `-y in slitPlane` and failed at ALL 199 points, making its theorem true and about nothing. Checking conditions one at a time would not have caught that; checking them together is the whole point

WHICH DISJUNCT carries `y in notCut`, classified by ROOT TYPE rather than by `Im != 0`. This matters: polyroots returns |Im| ~ 1e-41 for the REAL root, so a naive `Im != 0` test attributes it to the wrong disjunct. In exact arithmetic the real root is carried by Re < 1 and the complex pair by Im != 0 -- and a Lean proof must follow the exact split, not the numerical one
gates.misattribution_rate: 1 of 291 real roots (1 of 597 checks) -- rare enough that a spot check would miss it entirely

gates.claim: x*y and y/x are NEVER real on the arc -- both are carried by Im != 0 at every one of the 597 checks, with a genuine margin rather than a near-miss. So their notCut membership needs no case split at all, unlike `y`'s. This is the cheapest part of VSide to prove and `exists_pinning_data` already supplies part of it: it gives (x*y_3).im < 0, and (x*y_2).im < 0 when c < 0

WHAT A LEAN PROOF NEEDS, per condition -- with every clause MEASURED. (1) y != 0, x*y != 0, y/x != 0: the product of the three roots is -d/a = 1 identically in x, so no root can vanish; measured below as |y1*y2*y3 - 1| and as a lower bound on |y|. (2) x*y and y/x in notCut: via Im != 0, no case split (G3), and exists_pinning_data already supplies a sign -- measured below as the per-arc-point count of roots with (x*y).im < 0. (3) y in notCut: THE ONLY ONE NEEDING A CASE SPLIT -- real root via Re = t < 1, complex pair via Im != 0 (G2)
gates.hardest_condition: y in notCut -- the only one needing a real/complex case split
already_available: gamma_rel: t*(t^2 - 2ct + 2c + 1) = 1, so no root is 0

gates.claim: THE ARC CROSSES THE DISCRIMINANT, and no real root reaches 1. On |x| = 1 the y-cubic is `unitCubic (Re x)` with REAL coefficients, so the roots are all-real or one-real-plus-conjugate-pair. Both regimes occur on the arc -- so `continuous_otherRoots`'s collision branch is exercised, not defensive, and the real branch of `y in notCut` must cover three roots at some arc points. Separately: shifting t = 1 + s gives unitCubic c (1+s) = 1 + (4-2c)s + (3-2c)s^2 + s^3, whose coefficients are ALL POSITIVE for c <= 1, so no root reaches 1 -- a uniform Re < 1 needing no `exists_pinning_data`

verdict.measured: VSide is NON-VACUOUS: all six conditions hold simultaneously at all 597 checks (199 arc points x 3 roots).
verdict.trap_avoided: a naive `Im != 0` disjunct attribution counts the REAL root as complex, because polyroots returns |Im| ~ 1e-41 for it. Classified by root type instead. The non-vacuity conclusion is unaffected; the REASON it holds -- which is what a proof needs -- was contaminated.
verdict.structural_surprise: 291 real roots over 199 arc points, not 199 -- at 46 of them ALL THREE roots are real. The arc crosses the discriminant at c* = -0.74221766588, so `continuous_otherRoots`'s collision branch is live, and the real branch of `y in notCut` must cover three roots at some points. G5.
verdict.still_open: the Lean proof of VSide, plus concrete Y_1 Y_2 Y_3 and the two log(-y) routes. Everything else in Gap A is proved.
